title: Hardware Generation with High Flexibility using Reinforcement Learning Enhanced LLMs
problem: RTL design requires early commitment to Power, Performance, and Area (PPA) trade-offs; engineers often discover mismatches only after synthesis, necessitating costly iterative redesigns.
motivation: LLMs show promise for hardware generation but lack mechanisms to optimize for specific PPA objectives; flexible, goal-driven design automation is essential for modern chip design.
method: The tool uses an AI language model trained with reinforcement learning—where the model learns from reward signals—to generate hardware designs (RTL). After each generated design is converted to a circuit (synthesis), the tool measures the actual power consumption, speed, and chip area (PPA metrics) and feeds these measurements back as rewards to guide the model. This teaches the model to generate designs that hit specific optimization targets instead of discovering mismatches only after costly synthesis runs.
key_novelty: The core idea is using measured power, performance, and area results from synthesized designs as direct learning feedback to teach the AI model which designs to generate, rather than treating those measurements as a separate evaluation step.
contributions: Reinforcement learning framework coupling LLMs with post-synthesis PPA metrics as rewards
Support for single and multi-objective PPA optimization (Power, Performance, Area, or combinations)
Demonstrated applicability across various application scenarios and project constraints

metrics.ppa: improved PPA trade-offs across various optimization objectives

limitations: Not discussed—focus on reward design without hardware implementation constraints.
primary_theme: LLM-based RTL generation with RL-guided PPA optimization
